# p105 — Naval telegram acknowledgments

**Reading layers:** [Raw output · Edited output · Readable German · Conditional interpretation](../docs/reading-conventions.md). In decoded streams, `?` marks one unresolved position; `X` and numeral/letter labels remain literal.

[Case index](README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../README.md)

**Status:** Earlier raw body reproduced exactly; repaired stream still has an unpaired coordinate. **Key:** `Nov1-3`.

**Earliest credited record:** [Norbert, 2017-03-01, comment 15](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-852622). **Current source and arithmetic review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 2 November 2026.

## Most likely reading

**Readable German — earlier credited reconstruction, with unresolved fields retained:**

> Germania-[Etappe] Konstantinopel. Fuer [Mittelmeerdivision]. Zu [Tel. Nr.] 62, [Div.-Telegr. Nr.] 58: […] 32141 Q4 A vom 4. November [erledigt]. [Admiralstab]. 32398 B.

**Meaning:** A message for the Mediterranean naval division, routed through the Germania staging organization in Constantinople, reports that a matter in earlier telegrams has been dealt with. The intervening reference wording is damaged.

**Notes:** Brackets mark editorial interpretations of garbled words. The reference numbers are retained without attempting to reconstruct their administrative meaning. Baertl's longer completion is printed below for attribution; its extra wording is not recovered by the 143-letter model. The final unpaired coordinate and its optional deletion are separately certified.

## Recomputed reading

Variant `norbert15`: Exact 2017 repair and decoded paired prefix; odd final coordinate retained.

**Recomputed prior reading — under the recorded variant and repairs:**

```text
GERMANIAATAPPEKONSTANTINOPELXRFUERMITTEHMEERDIVIC9VNZUXTEL9VRX62XDOV2TTELEGRXN0X58XISTELTX32141XQ4XAXVOMX4CNOVEMBERNULEDIGTXA8MIRALSTAFX32398XB
```

## Review

- The scan's groups 46/47 are DGGVF and XGDGD. Legacy web groups FGGVF/XGXAD introduce three spurious coordinate differences.
- Deleting three coordinates from 290 gives 287. The last intermediate D is preserved as an explicit undecoded suffix, not silently discarded.

## Earlier published readings

**Raw decryption — [Norbert, 2017-03-01, comment 15](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-852622).**

Same text as the recomputed reading above.

**Editorial completion — [Max Baertl, 2017-03-01, comment 16](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-852648); [Max Baertl, 2017-03-01, comment 17](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-852655); [Max Baertl, 2017-03-11, comment 39](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-858010).**

**Earlier attributed reading:**

```text
GERMANIAETAPPEKONSTANTINOPELXXFUERMITTELMEERDIVISIONZUXTELXNRX62XDIVXTELEGRXNRX58XERSTELLTX32141XQ4XANX32141XQ4XAXVOMX4XNOVEMBERERLEDIGTXADMIRALSTABX32398XB
```

Published length 156; model length 143.

## Verified variants

| Variant | Fixed / total positions | Unpaired suffix | Ordinary re-encryption |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `norbert15` | 143 / 143 | D | Partial |
| `norbert15_with_explicit_orphan_deletion` | 143 / 143 | — | Yes |

Source strings, edit positions, plaintext domains and attribution are retained in [the prior-reading certificate](../data/prior_readings.json). Re-encryption checks the stated reconstruction, including any conjectural repairs.

## Explicit repair of the orphan coordinate

The unpaired final intermediate `D` comes from original source index **244** (the 245th received character, final `D` of group 49 `XAXGD`). Deleting it in addition to the three published deletions produces 286 coordinates and exactly the same 143-letter body, now with a complete ordinary re-encryption. This equivalent reconstruction is a contribution of the present arithmetic review; it does not establish the historical error mechanism.

# p215 — Entente fleet report and Corps Kosch interpretation

**Reading layers:** [Raw output · Edited output · Readable German · Conditional interpretation](../docs/reading-conventions.md). In decoded streams, `?` marks one unresolved position; `X` and numeral/letter labels remain literal.

[Case index](README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../README.md)

**Status:** Earlier partial reading verified exactly; a new conditional interpretation identifies Corps Kosch. A separate unit-based numeral hypothesis constrains the closing field to `?1?6`. A fluent complete plaintext remains unsupported. **Key:** `Nov22-24`.

**Earliest credited record:** [Norbert, 2017-03-03, comment 32](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-853562). **Current source and arithmetic review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 2 November 2026.

## Most likely partial interpretation

**Readable German — earlier partial interpretation under the stated geometry:**

> […] [Kertsch]. Bringt [Ententeflotte] zwo [Divisionen] — [Neuseelaender],
> Engl. u. [Franzo] — mit. [Nur] OHL, [Korps Kosch]. 3Y52.

**Meaning:** The damaged report connects Kerch with an Entente fleet bringing two divisions, described as New Zealanders, English and French. The closing words may restrict circulation to the Supreme Army Command and Corps Kosch. This translates the proposed report; it does not establish that those troops actually arrived or that its nationalities and numbers were accurate. The opening remains unresolved. The closing field has baseline labels `3Y52`; the separate historical numeral hypothesis below gives `?1?6`, without identifying a particular reference number.

**Notes:** Brackets mark interpretations requiring fills or changed known coordinates; all punctuation is editorial. `Franzo` remains an abbreviation. The proposed 92-character segment from `KERTSCH` through the separator after `KOSCH` needs **nine known-coordinate changes and fifteen fills** under Norbert's two-gap geometry. Eight fills concern printed erasures and seven concern the inserted gaps. This is a narrower, explicitly costed proposal, not a repair of the whole message.

### Why Corps Kosch is the preferred closing interpretation

| Reading of raw `KOR1S??OSCH` | Known-coordinate changes | Erasure fills |
|---|---:|---:|
| `KORPSXKOSCH` | 2 | 2 |
| Earlier `KORPSFRISCH` | 5 | 2 |

The Kosch reading changes original coordinate 22 from `X` to `V` and 193 from
`D` to `X`, then fills two inserted gaps. The proposed separator is outside
the raw letter domain; it is not supplied merely by choosing an erased symbol.
A 29 April 1918 naval directive identifies Kosch as German commander in Crimea,
and Hopman's November diary places him in the same operational setting.
The [coordinate and historical review](../experiments/p215_context/README.md)
gives the exact maps, primary-document references and remaining limits.

Baertl's earlier full proposal still requires at least **27** changes to known
coordinates, even after optimizing its extra-letter deletion and insertion
geometry. The separately retained language-ranked completions are compatible
with the source under their stated model; they do not recover new historical
letters.

## Separate late-key numeral interpretation

The [source-reviewed p217 operational report](other/p217_A.md) and contemporary formation evidence support a consistent optional Nov22–24 map: baseline `Y→1`, `J→2`, `2→6`. Applying exactly that map here gives **`?1?6`** at the end, with no change to a received coordinate or to Norbert’s gap geometry. The other unproved digit and rare-letter labels are cleared before this map is applied, preserving a single injective square.

More precisely, the ending is `a1b6`, with different `a` and `b` from `0345789JQY`. All **90** combinations have source-preserving global witnesses. An additional all-numerical-reference assumption leaves **42** candidates, allowing a leading zero. This does not select a serial number or fill any of the 21 unknown coordinates. The [propagation certificate](../experiments/late_key_interpretation/README.md) retains the original baseline output, the conditional domains and the exact source indices.

## Recomputed reading

Variant `norbert32`: Exact published partial geometry; no inserted coordinate is guessed.

**Recomputed prior reading — under the recorded variant and repairs:**

```text
ABSXMI?I5XNA6M?LD?XS4NXS4?XN?R?DAKER?SC?XBRINGTENT?N?EFLHTTEZWO?IVI?IONENX?EUSRELAEND?RXENGLXUXF?ATZ?XMITXN??OHLXKOR1S??OSCHX3Y52
```

## Review

- The primary 248-slot transcript has 237 known coordinates and 11 erasures. Two inserted unknown groups increase the geometry to 258 slots.
- The model fixes 109 of 129 plaintext positions and leaves 6^21 compatible completions under the fixed complete square.
- Baertl's 130-letter editorial text has the wrong length for this geometry. Even its best single-letter deletion contradicts 27 known coordinates at 20 plaintext positions.

## Earlier published readings

**Partial raw decryption — [Norbert, 2017-03-03, comment 32](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-853562).**

Same text as the recomputed reading above.

**Editorial completion — [Max Baertl, 2017-03-11, comment 39](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-858010).**

**Earlier attributed reading:**

```text
ABSXMIDIV5XEILMELDGX24NX24NXARMADAKERTSCHXBRINGTENTENTEFLOTTEZWODIVISIONENXNEUSEELAENDERXENGLXUXFRANZOXMITXNUROHLXKORPSFRISCHX3Y52
```

Published length 130; model length 129.

## Verified variants

| Variant | Fixed / total positions | Unpaired suffix | Ordinary re-encryption |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `norbert32` | 109 / 129 | — | Partial |

Source strings, edit positions, plaintext domains and attribution are retained in [the prior-reading certificate](../data/prior_readings.json). Re-encryption checks the stated reconstruction, including any conjectural repairs.

## Full uncertainty audit

The [p215 constraint certificate](../data/certificates/p215.json) verifies all 21 unresolved coordinates under the two-group insertion model. It yields exactly **21,936,950,640,377,856** compatible plaintexts. Exhaustively deleting each possible single letter from Baertl's longer wording still requires at least **27 changes to received coordinates**, affecting **20 plaintext positions**. Run `python3 -m adfgvx.constraints215` to reproduce the comparison.

Source: [Childs p215 C](../sources/excerpts/childs_p215_C.png).

## Source-compatible model completions

The [exact completion experiment](../experiments/p215_completion/README.md) retains the ten highest-ranked strings under each of three language objectives. All thirty preserve every one of the 237 known source coordinates under Norbert's two-gap geometry. These are conditional completions, not recovered historical letters; the source still permits 6^21 strings.

The [broader insertion-geometry audit](../experiments/p215_completion/README.md#broader-audit-of-the-earlier-editorial-text)
shows that the best one-letter deletion of Baertl's completion still needs at
least 27 known-coordinate changes even when all ten inserted coordinates may
be placed anywhere. This strengthens the earlier fixed-gap comparison without
accepting a different plaintext or corruption model.
headings: # p215 — Entente fleet report and Corps Kosch interpretation
### Why Corps Kosch is the preferred closing interpretation

# p198 — Open CHI intercept with a length shortfall

**Reading layers:** [Raw output · Edited output · Readable German · Conditional interpretation](../docs/reading-conventions.md). In decoded streams, `?` marks one unresolved position; `X` and numeral/letter labels remain literal.

[All cases](README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../README.md)

**Status:** No accepted plaintext. **Current source and attack review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. Original challenge: [Lasry–Schmeh](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/unsolved-adfxvx-messages-from-world-war-i/).

## Most likely reading

No defensible plaintext has yet been identified. The source and the best tested hypotheses are recorded below; no language-ranked diagnostic is promoted to a historical reading.

| Source fact | Value |
|---|---|
| Printed page / PDF page | 198 / 201 |
| Section | D |
| Received slots | 165 |
| Valid coordinates / uncertain slots | 165 / 0 |
| Header | `PZU v CM (18.27 p.m., November 15th); 18.45; CHI-170` |

## Literal ciphertext

**Source transcription:**

```text
DFVXV XGAXD GXVXD VGVGD VADXF FADVX XXVFV AAXGF DGFFA VXAVV
VXVFV GFVFG DGVFG FFFGV VVGGG XVFXF XXFVD VDFDD FXAAX VVXAA
FXXXV GXFVD VVXXF FGXGV FGXFG GFAAA FGXVV FXXXF FADXD AFXFV
VDGVX FGAGF ADDFX
```

The [catalog](../data/messages.json) retains the literal source, conservative analysis layer, and earlier online transcription separately. Headers follow `recipient v sender`.

## Length qualification

The header advertises **CHI-170**, while the body contains **165 valid coordinates**. No erased group is explicitly printed. A single five-coordinate loss is a plausible model, but the source does not establish its location or contiguity. Ordinary complete ADFGVX requires an even coordinate count; silent truncation is not accepted.

This challenge target is **section D**. The separately readable
[p198 C transport message](context/transport.md) and the newly linked
[p198 B/E equipment and lorry orders](context/transport_197_198.md) use the
`RIZI` identifier and do not solve this `CHI` entry. Section E contains one
extra five-coordinate group, but moving that group into D is only a tested
corruption hypothesis, not an established source repair.

## Attack status

No accepted plaintext. Bounded missing-group and component-reuse searches preserve the 165 valid coordinates under their declared length hypotheses. [The experiment index](../experiments/README.md) records completed scopes and controls. Unknown keys, noncontiguous losses, other corruption models, and header errors remain unexcluded.

### Exact scattered-loss experiments

The [marginal decoder](../experiments/p198_exact_sparse/README.md) covers all
**1,115,034,284** possible positions of five scattered losses for each supplied
complete key. The [joint decoder](../experiments/p198_joint_exact/README.md)
also chooses their six-valued coordinates consistently, covering
**8,670,506,592,384 loss-and-fill witnesses**. The latter count includes aliases;
it does not count distinct plaintexts.

The recorded historical runs fix one transposition and one heuristic
completion of each of two partial squares. Neither gives a readable result.
The joint four-gram objective also selects wrong plaintexts in both synthetic
controls even when supplied with the true complete keys. The source witnesses,
exact scores and failures are retained. These experiments resolve the search
optimum under their stated assumptions; they do not establish a historical key,
validate the damage model, or solve p198.

The [six-gram calibration](../experiments/p198_joint_six/README.md) does recover
one complete 85-letter control, including its exact loss mask and fills, under
both pure-six and mixed objectives. A feasible wrong competitor still beats
the other control's truth under both objectives. This improves the demonstrated
capability of the method while preserving its remaining scoring limitation.

The subsequent [historical pure-six run](../experiments/p198_six_historical/README.md)
under the frozen CHI13 completion changes the best geometry and improves its
six-gram objective, but the full result remains unreadable. At that selected
geometry, the conservative partial square has 48 singleton positions; this is
a conditional diagnostic, not 48 newly recovered letters. The report keeps
the entire model output and its disagreements with four-gram ranking.

### Exact constraints without a language model

An independent [letter-count bound](../experiments/p198_letter_bounds/README.md)
covers **all 40,320 completions** of the partial Nov13–15b square, with its
recorded transposition and every five-loss placement/fill. The attainable
ordinary-letter counts range from 44 to 82, so this family requires at least
three digits among the 85 plaintext positions. This is a modest exact
constraint without a language model; the actual message's digit count is
unknown, so it does not reject the key.

A stronger [category audit](../experiments/p198_letter_bounds/CATEGORY_BOUNDS.md)
gives `digits + Q + Y ≥ 10` throughout the same partial-key family. If a proposed
plaintext contains no Q or Y, it must therefore contain at least ten digits;
a witness attains that bound. A separate Python algorithm factors the problem
into adjacent-column pairs and fully recomputes the optimum, independently of
the original C++ decoder. Neither inequality assumes that the historical text
had a particular digit or Q/Y count.

The complete [digit/Q/Y frontier](../experiments/p198_category_frontier/README.md)
sharpens those separate inequalities. The following count pairs are attainable,
and every other attainable pair has at least as many digits and Q/Y positions
as one of these:

| Digit positions | Minimum Q/Y positions at that digit count |
|---:|---:|
| 3 | 13 |
| 4 | 6 |
| 5 | 5 |
| 6 | 4 |
| 7 | 3 |
| 8 | 2 |
| 9 | 1 |
| 10 | 0 |

Thus **three digits force at least thirteen Q/Y occurrences**, rather than
the seven allowed by the separate inequalities alone. Every frontier point
has a complete source-preserving witness. Two separate algorithms exhaust
all 28 letter/digit membership classes and their 15,504 loss allocations;
285,264 short exhaustive witnesses include an explicit control with two
incomparable count pairs. Different points may require different square
completions. These exact counts constrain future proposals within this
family; they do not supply a readable historical message or reject the key.

### Conditional restriction from an independently attested name

The [Tiflis appointment](other/tiflis_appointment.md) supplies a separate
historical-name argument for **Nov13–15b FX = Y**. If that inference and the
Nov13b/five-loss hypothesis for p198 are both accepted, the exact family
shrinks to 5,040 complete squares. Its digit/QY frontier is
`(4,6), (5,5), (6,4), (7,3), (8,2), (10,1), (13,0)`.
Thus at least four digits are required, or at least thirteen if the reading
contains no Q or Y. The [conditional certificate](../experiments/contextual_key_constraints/README.md)
preserves all received coordinates, supplies witnesses for every frontier
point, and independently recomputes all seven retained membership classes.
Neither the historical counts nor this key's applicability to p198 are
established. No plaintext position becomes fixed from this count result.

### Why individual positions remain open

For either frozen complete-key hypothesis, **each of the 85 positions can
contain any of the 36 alphabet symbols in some compatible five-loss witness**.
The construction marks that position's two ciphertext coordinates as lost,
puts the remaining three losses elsewhere, and fills the selected pair with
the desired character. Every received coordinate still appears unchanged and
in order.

The [constructive domain audit](../experiments/p198_letter_bounds/domain_witnesses.json)
checks all **6,120** key/position/symbol witnesses and exact re-encryption.
Each choice can use a different witness; arbitrary choices at all positions
need not coexist in one plaintext. That is why full individual domains can
coexist with the joint requirement of at least three digits. Additional source
evidence about the missing positions could narrow those domains.

```sh
python3 experiments/p198_letter_bounds/domain_witnesses.py --verify
```

The [direct source-similarity search](../experiments/source_similarity/README.md)
also checks all 788 extracted OCR blocks. Its leading p198 candidate is p154 A2;
independent page inspection confirms only a short local resemblance and does
not establish a parallel transmission.

# p187 — Monitoring Russian and Polish army traffic

**Reading layers:** [Raw output · Edited output · Readable German · Conditional interpretation](../docs/reading-conventions.md). In decoded streams, `?` marks one unresolved position; `X` and numeral/letter labels remain literal.

[Case index](README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../README.md)

**Status:** Earlier joint key recovery verified; incomplete substitution square and residual garbles preserved. **Key:** `CHI-Nov13`.

**Earliest credited record:** [George Lasry, 2017-05-03, comment 50](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-878059). **Current source and arithmetic review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 2 November 2026.

Norbert proposed the shared-key attack in comment 49; George Lasry recovered the key in comment 50; Norbert refined the labels in comment 53.

## Most likely reading

**Readable German — earlier credited word normalization:**

> [Russischen] und poln. Heeresverkehr voll erfassen. Wichtiges, besonders aus poln. Verkehr, ueber O.H.L.-Station verziffert funken.

**Meaning:** Monitor Russian and Polish army communications in full. Radio important material, especially from Polish traffic, in encrypted form via the Supreme Army Command station.

**Notes:** `poln.` means Polish; `O.H.L.` refers to Supreme Army Command. The source-derived first word ends in `T`, so `RUSSISCHEN` is Norbert's one-letter editorial normalization. The rest of this presentation supplies word divisions and punctuation. The order continues in [p187b](p187b.md).

## Recomputed reading

Variant `audited_CHI_direct`: No received-coordinate edits; only directly attested substitution cells are used.

**Raw output — recomputed direct CHI reading; attested cells only:**

```text
RUSSISCHETUNDPOLNHEERESVERKEHRVOLLERFASSENXWICHTIGESBESONDERSAUSPOLNVERKEHRUEBEROHLSTATIONVERZIFFERTFUNKEN
```

## Review

- Norbert first proposed the shared-key attack in comment 49 on 2017-04-30; George Lasry recovered the key in comment 50 on 2017-05-03; Norbert refined symbol labels in comment 53 the same day.
- The two received texts contain 354 coordinates, 177 plaintext slots. The initial combined publication has 173 letters and incorrectly describes 356 coordinates; four ending slots are not covered by that published string.
- Fourteen square cells remain unassigned. In particular j/x labels were suggested to be digits, not proved to be 0/01.

## Earlier published readings

**Initial substitution labels — [George Lasry, 2017-05-03, comment 50](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-878059).**

**Earlier attributed reading:**

```text
RUSSISCHETUNDPOLNHEERESVERGEHRVOLLERFASSENKWICHTIMESBESONDERSAUSPOLNVERGEHRUEBEROHLSTATIONVERZIFFERTFUNGEN
```

**Refined partial substitution labels — [Norbert, 2017-05-03, comment 53](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-878079).**

Same text as the recomputed reading above.

**Editorial normalization — [Norbert, 2017-05-03, comment 53](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-878079).**

**Earlier attributed reading:**

```text
RUSSISCHENUNDPOLNHEERESVERKEHRVOLLERFASSENXWICHTIGESBESONDERSAUSPOLNVERKEHRUEBEROHLSTATIONVERZIFFERTFUNKEN
```

Conflicts at 1 plaintext position under the compared variant.

## Verified variants

| Variant | Fixed / total positions | Unpaired suffix | Ordinary re-encryption |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `audited_CHI_direct` | 106 / 106 | — | Yes |

Source strings, edit positions, plaintext domains and attribution are retained in [the prior-reading certificate](../data/prior_readings.json). Re-encryption checks the stated reconstruction, including any conjectural repairs.

# p187b — Teleprinter failure and written reporting

**Reading layers:** [Raw output · Edited output · Readable German · Conditional interpretation](../docs/reading-conventions.md). In decoded streams, `?` marks one unresolved position; `X` and numeral/letter labels remain literal.

[Case index](README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../README.md)

**Status:** Earlier joint key recovery verified; a single adjacent-coordinate swap explains two prior editorial word corrections. The incomplete ending remains unresolved. **Key:** `CHI-Nov13`.

**Earliest credited record:** [George Lasry, 2017-05-03, comment 50](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-878059). **Current source and arithmetic review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 2 November 2026.

Norbert proposed the shared-key attack in comment 49; George Lasry recovered the key in comment 50; Norbert refined the labels in comment 53.

## Most likely reading

**Readable German — earlier word normalization explained by the separately costed swap:**

> Soweit Fernschreiber-Verbdg. [nicht arbeitet], Rest schriftlich. `NACHCHEF?X??????`.

**Meaning:** Where the teleprinter connection is not working, provide the remainder in writing. The closing designation or reference beginning `NACHCHEF` remains incomplete.

**Notes:** `Verbdg.` abbreviates “connection.” Norbert normalized the raw `NITHT ARBEICET` to `NICHT ARBEITET` in 2017. The new coordinate audit below explains both changes with one adjacent swap. The seven unresolved ending positions are retained in full; no digit assignments are inferred from their administrative appearance. This continues the communications instruction in [p187](p187.md).

The literal closing field `NACHCHEF?X??????` retains all seven unresolved
positions and its known `X`. It is shown in full rather than using a display
omission for the last six positions. The bracketed words retain Norbert's
earlier normalization and the separately stated swap model below.

## Recomputed reading

Variant `audited_CHI_direct`: No received-coordinate edits; only directly attested substitution cells are used.

**Raw output — recomputed direct CHI reading; attested cells only:**

```text
SOWEITFERNSCHREIBERVERBDGNITHTARBEICETXRESTSCHRIFTLICHXNACHCHEF?X??????
```

## Conditional adjacent-swap repair

The printed 26th group is **`VDFAD`**. Swapping its last two coordinates gives
**`VDFDA`** and restores both previously proposed words:

![Original p187 A2 second part, with VDFAD in the bottom row](../sources/excerpts/childs_p187_A2_swap.png)

**Edited output — conditional adjacent-coordinate swap; unresolved ending retained:**

```text
SOWEITFERNSCHREIBERVERBDGNICHTARBEITETXRESTSCHRIFTLICHXNACHCHEF?X??????
```

Only received indices **128 and 129** change (`AD` → `DA`, zero-based).
All other **140 coordinates**, the coordinate counts, key and square remain
unchanged. These map to plaintext position 27 (`T` → `C`) and 35 (`C` → `T`).
The reading still has **64/71 fixed positions**; this repair resolves two
word garbles, not the unknown ending.

The [exhaustive adjacent-swap audit](../experiments/p187b_adjacent_swap/README.md)
checks all 141 such operations and finds exactly this one for the stated
partial reading. The historical cause of the reversal is unknown. The raw
source remains unaltered, and Norbert retains credit for the normalized words.

## Review

- Norbert first proposed the shared-key attack in comment 49 on 2017-04-30; George Lasry recovered the key in comment 50 on 2017-05-03; Norbert refined symbol labels in comment 53 the same day.
- The two received texts contain 354 coordinates, 177 plaintext slots. The initial combined publication has 173 letters and incorrectly describes 356 coordinates; four ending slots are not covered by that published string.
- Fourteen square cells remain unassigned. In particular j/x labels were suggested to be digits, not proved to be 0/01.

# Siegfried's assignment to the Military Mission is cancelled

**Reading layers:** [Raw output · Edited output · Readable German · Conditional interpretation](../../docs/reading-conventions.md). In decoded streams, `?` marks one unresolved position; `X` and numeral/letter labels remain literal.

**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The source's 401-coordinate frame yields a clear first portion followed by a
pairing-phase failure. A conditional surplus-X model recovers the rest of the
order, with an exact source-shaped forward witness. Its complete closing has
independent, unedited coordinate-pair support from the previously reviewed
Osthoff order. Neither the error model nor the shared formula assigns a
biographical identity to Siegfried or Marschall.

## p135 A

Childs p135, PDF p138; [source crop](../../experiments/siegfried_assignment_cancellation/sources/p135_A.png).
The page heading and internal date are 5 November, while reception is 7 November.
The key remains the published **Nov4–6** key.

**Source transcription — literal header:**

```text
5th NOVEMBER, 1918.
A) YZ v LP (8.59 a.m., November 7th)
FUER YZ 2400 (5/11)
RICHI-401
```

The scan contains **401 source slots**, exactly its printed `RICHI-401`:
397 valid coordinates and four printed dash slots. The original inverse
transposition leaves one final coordinate unpaired.

**Raw output — unaltered 401-coordinate frame, with its final orphan retained separately in the certificate:**

```text
DTSCHEMILITAERMISS?ONINKONSTANTINOPELXZUNR45610XKOMDODESOBERLTSSIEGFRIEDNACHDERTUERKEIDESZENZUTEILUNGZURMILITAEEMRSNYSL4N6FXRGA13FQLMUKV1B14IWUXRGETMF13WLJ66WL4Q?A1ONJQ1?ZT4NFKFW?EYNMLLLOGR6LZZL6JYETM
```

## A conditional surplus coordinate before transposition

The proposed error stage is precise: an extra observed **X** entered the
fractionated coordinate stream **before transposition**. After applying the
original 401-slot inverse transposition, excluding that X restores an even
400-coordinate paired stream. The received ciphertext is not shortened to
400 before inverse transposition.

Two adjacent interim X coordinates are indistinguishable under this model:

| Excluded interim position | Original received source position | Observed value |
|---:|---:|:---:|
|230|296|X|
|231|84|X|

Either exclusion gives the same 400-coordinate interim stream and the same
candidate source-shaped ciphertext. Both source-origin alternatives remain
in the certificate; no unique physical origin is asserted. The excluded X
is an observed coordinate with an explicit one-coordinate model cost, not a
free mask or an invisible omission from the source transcription.

**Raw output — conditional surplus-X exclusion at interim 230 or 231; 196/200 fixed positions:**

```text
DTSCHEMILITAERMISS?ONINKONSTANTINOPELXZUNR45610XKOMDODESOBERLTSSIEGFRIEDNACHDERTUERKEIDESZENZUTEILUNGZURMILITAEEMRSSIONISTAUFGEHOBENXAKOFOLGTXAUFALLERHOECHSTENB?FEHLCHEF?ILITAER?AHINETTSFGHTMARSCHALLX
```

**Edited output — same declared model, seven observed-coordinate substitutions and four printed-mask fills; 200/200 fixed positions:**

```text
DTSCHEMILITAERMISSIONINKONSTANTINOPELXZUNR45610XKOMDODESOBERLTSSIEGFRIEDNACHDERTUERKEIDESSENZUTEILUNGZURMILITAERMISSIONISTAUFGEHOBENXAKOFOLGTXAUFALLERHOECHSTENBEFEHLCHEFMILITAERKABINETTSFRHRMARSCHALLX
```

Observed substitutions, with zero-based received source indices: **127 F→X**, **186 A→V**, **187 V→A**, **225 F→V**, **258 X→V**, **293 V→G**, **367 A→X**.

Printed-mask fills: **42→A**, **43→X**, **44→F**, **167→V**.

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Dtsche Militaermission in Konstantinopel. Zu Nr 45610. Komdo des Oberlts Siegfried nach der Tuerkei, dessen Zuteilung zur Militaermission ist aufgehoben. AKO folgt. Auf allerhoechsten Befehl Chef Militaerkabinetts Frhr Marschall.

**Meaning:** Regarding 45610 and the posting of Oberleutnant Siegfried to Turkey, the message cancels his assignment to the Military Mission. AKO follows. It closes with the Chief of the Military Cabinet formula and FRHR MARSCHALL. The message does not report a completed return journey or establish a separate biographical identity.

The original reference **45610** and the abbreviations **DTSCHE**, **KOMDO**,
**OBERLTS**, **AKO** and **FRHR** remain literal in the reading. No digit is
relabelled, and no abbreviation is expanded into an independently asserted
person or document.

## Exact forward witness and bounded stage comparison

To reconstruct the actual source shape:

1. Fractionate the proposed 200-character plaintext with the unchanged square.
2. Reinsert the observed surplus X at interim 230 or 231, restoring 401 coordinates.
3. Transpose those 401 coordinates with the unchanged column ranks.
4. Compare with the literal source: exactly seven observed substitutions and
   four dash fills remain, and no received source position has been deleted.

This replay succeeds for both aliases. Ordinary encryption of the 200-letter
proposal into a 400-coordinate ciphertext is not presented as the source
witness; the declared surplus stage is part of the verified reconstruction.

All single-coordinate exclusions at both relevant stages were priced against
the same complete proposed text:

| Model stage | Candidates examined | Minimum observed substitutions | Minimum positions | Mask fills at minima | Observed surplus/excluded coordinates |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
|After inverse transposition of the 401-slot source|401|7|Interim 230 or 231|4|1|
|From the received ciphertext before inverse transposition|401|144|Source 297, 298 or 299|4|1|

The comparison favors the declared stage within this fixed-template,
single-coordinate family. It does not prove what happened historically,
exclude multi-error explanations, or turn the whole tail into a direct
ordinary-frame decoding.

## Independent support for the complete closing

The last **58 plaintext positions**, beginning `AUFALLERHOECHSTENBEFEHL`,
match the direct raw closing of [p149 A2](osthoff.md). That older physical
record has its own [source crop](../../experiments/corpus_attack/sources/childs_p149_A2.png),
which was reviewed again for this comparison. The new certificate checks
all 58 coordinate pairs, their letters and both sets of source positions.

This supports the repairs in `BEFEHL`, `MILITAERKABINETTS` and `FRHR` without
inventing a smoother signature from general historical expectations. The
parallel concerns Osthoff, so its other body words and identity are not
transferred to Siegfried's order. It is not counted as another newly recovered
record.

## Attribution and evidence

The published key and previously reviewed Osthoff source retain their
original attribution. Earlier unreviewed OCR screens for p135 are frozen
separately; their garbled output is not treated as a primary transcription.
This edition supplies source review, the explicit surplus-coordinate model,
both aliases, finite stage prices and the complete qualified reading. It
makes no historical first-decipherment claim.

[prior screens](../../experiments/siegfried_assignment_cancellation/prior_candidates.json)
and [reproduction](../../experiments/siegfried_assignment_cancellation/README.md)
provide the complete evidence.
